cases.title: A confident answer from incomplete evidence
cases.short_input: Can the booked 17:10 ferry and connecting shuttle reach the workshop before check-in closes?
cases.reference_conclusion: No. The ferry reaches the landing at 17:40. The shuttle departs at 17:45 and takes 12 minutes, arriving at 17:57. Check-in closes at 17:55.
cases.finding: The agent published a confident positive answer after one search. It did not request any full document. Its stated 17:50 arrival was unsupported; the 12-minute shuttle journey was outside the returned excerpt.
cases.next_question: Can evidence-aware investigation reduce unsupported conclusions without forcing every answer through a fixed sequence?
cases.scenario_type: Authored synthetic development scenario, not a transcript from real audio.

cases.title: Repeated searches without a useful answer
cases.short_input: Can a browser-only setup save camera and screen recordings as two separate files if a paid plan is allowed?
cases.reference_conclusion: No. Browser recording creates one combined video on every plan. Separate files require the installed desktop recorder, which the conversation rules out.
cases.finding: The agent made 15 searches and 14 waits, but did not read a full document or publish a card. It stopped after exceeding the soft token budget.
cases.next_question: Can the harness help the agent recognize when repeated search is no longer adding evidence, and move toward a supported conclusion?

reference_evidence_verbatim.title: LumenCast browser workshop camera and shared-screen recording
reference_evidence_verbatim.text: LumenCast browser workshop recording creates one combined video containing the camera and shared screen. This browser mode does not save independent camera and screen files on any plan. The recording download preserves that combined layout; changing the subscription does not add separate tracks to a browser recording. This article describes the browser recorder, not the desktop recorder.

reference_evidence_verbatim.title: LumenCast desktop recorder independent camera and screen files
reference_evidence_verbatim.text: LumenCast Desktop Recorder can save the camera video and shared-screen video as two independent files. That capture mode requires installing and running the desktop recorder on the recording computer before the workshop. It is not a browser setting and cannot split an already combined browser recording into the original independent streams.

reference_evidence_verbatim.title: LumenCast plans and browser workshop recording features
reference_evidence_verbatim.text: LumenCast paid plans increase workshop recording duration and storage allowances. They do not change the browser recorder's combined camera-and-screen format. Independent camera and shared-screen files are a capability of the installed desktop recorder. Paying for a plan by itself does not enable that desktop capture mode in a browser.

planned_asr.intro: The next experiments will test whether the harness remains useful when conversation text comes from real speech recognition.

questions.title: Stable conversation state
questions.hypothesis: Keeping the latest text for each speech segment, while preserving its revision history, may reduce decisions based on superseded partial transcripts.
questions.test: Replay the same conversation as a corrected transcript and as the original ASR event stream. Compare useful help, incorrect help and stale cards.

questions.title: Revision or new intent?
questions.hypothesis: Distinguishing an ASR rewrite from a person changing their request may reduce unnecessary investigation changes.
questions.test: Include unchanged meaning, corrected names or numbers, and genuine changes of intent. Score mistaken revisions separately.

questions.title: When to investigate
questions.hypothesis: Selective investigation of incomplete speech may reduce wasted retrieval without delaying useful help too much.
questions.test: Compare the current baseline with the modified harness under the same model and resource limits; measure missed help, repeated work and help latency.

planned_asr.disclosure: These are research hypotheses and proposed tests, not implemented capabilities or measured improvements.

recovery_finding.text: The optional recovery prompt fired zero times across all 18 runs. Scripted tests validate the mechanism, but this batch cannot establish its effect on answer quality or cost.

investigation_progress.problem: Choosing whether to continue investigating, change approach, publish help, or stay silent.

finding.headline: Lower cost. No increase in useful help.
finding.interpretation: Both configurations delivered useful help in 5 of 14 required-help runs and passed all 6 silence-control runs. Progress feedback reduced token use by 16.7% and material-error runs from 3 to 1, but runs ending with no active help card increased from 6 to 8. The current baseline remains the reference; the new mechanism is experimental.
trace_findings: The same aggregate help score hides different outcomes. Across the seven help scenarios, progress feedback improved the two-repeat score on two scenarios, reduced it on three, and tied on two. The three silence scenarios tied.

The progress message was present in all 143 treatment model requests and in none of the control requests. Its largest observed size was 2,110 characters. There was no automatic context-summary call in this held-out batch. This verifies exposure to the intervention, not that the model used it correctly.

Exact repeated queries fell from four to zero; full-read arrivals fell from 45 to 26. These behavior changes did not improve total useful help. Eight of the fourteen treatment help runs ended with no active card, compared with six in the baseline.

In both RillStat treatment runs, the full guide arrived and the final private response correctly distinguished an ordinary difference test from equivalence. Neither run called publish_card. These two inspected traces establish a delivery failure; they do not imply that all eight no-card runs had a correct answer ready.

Two grading boundaries remain explicit, both in baseline runs: a correct conceptual explanation based on the dialogue, and a hedged but unsupported admission guess. Alternative treatment of these boundaries gives the baseline 4 to 6 help successes versus the treatment's 5. The small study therefore does not support a clear quality improvement.

The next focused comparison should examine ending and delivery decisions: distinguish justified silence from a useful conclusion that stays private or a valid card that is withdrawn without new evidence. It should preserve the agent's choice to stay silent and avoid automatically publishing private working text. This follow-up has not been implemented or evaluated.
finding.promotion_decision: Keep the progress configuration opt-in; no useful-help improvement demonstrated.
finding.uncertainty: 10 newly authored synthetic scenarios, two repeats, one local model, AI-only assessment. No statistical significance or real-conversation benefit is claimed.

analysis.rating_source: Provided semantic ratings; no automatic content grading.

metric_definitions.exact_duplicate_query_count: Additional exact query-string occurrences in the durable tool ledger, including failed attempts; no lowercasing or whitespace normalization.
metric_definitions.full_read_arrival_count: Environment read-result arrivals containing text; repeated full reads count separately.
metric_definitions.card_count: Active cards at the saved final observation; distinct from publication/update event count.
metric_definitions.model_requests_with_progress: Saved model requests containing the dedicated human message ID and JSON kind; summary text merely mentioning progress is not counted.
metric_definitions.summary_model_calls: Role-labelled summarization calls or a single human-message request exactly matching the pinned Deep Agents default summary prompt prefix and suffix. Custom unlabelled summarizers may be missed. No private model content is copied to this report.
metric_definitions.missed_help: Rated help runs that fail the final primary criterion, including missing, incorrect or unsupported help; overlaps any_material_error_runs.
metric_definitions.any_material_error_runs: Separate reviewer flag for any material error, including a transient error later corrected; it does not overwrite the final primary judgment.
metric_definitions.model_wall_ms: Sum of recorded model-call wall time, not end-to-end audio latency.

boundary_decisions.reason: The stated difference test and missing equivalence analysis allow a general conceptual distinction; this is not an invented fictional-product fact. Keep the reviewers uncertainty and show a conservative sensitivity score treating it as unsuccessful.

scoring_audit.policy: No heldout-specific implementation or rubric changes; retain original judgments and explicit scoring-boundary sensitivity.

protocol_freeze.treatment_decision: Measure the original factual projection, including null or adverse effects; no selection based on held-out outcomes.

studies.title: Missing needs and invented needs
studies.sample_plain: 24 short dialogues, 2 models, 2 prompts, 2 repeats; 192 calls.
studies.finding_plain: Coverage reminders reduced missed needs for 9B, but added invented needs. For 14B, misses stayed at zero while invented needs rose from 2 to 8.
limits: Recognition only; no retrieval, answer delivery or full agent run.

method_notes: Both prompts used the same dialogue, local model settings and free-form output.
Each condition has 48 outputs and 56 reference-need appearances: 28 annotated needs, repeated twice.

studies.sample_plain: 4 meetings, 2 models, 3 harnesses, 2 repeats; 48 run attempts.
studies.finding_plain: Complete help rose from 0 to 4 of 6 runs for 14B, and from 0 to 3 of 6 for 9B. All 16 repair runs received the full dialogue; some updates still failed.

method_notes: All three harnesses were rerun in the same batch for each unchanged local model.

Recognition probes are separate from the running agent.

studies.title: Reviewing private answers for delivery
studies.sample_plain: 3 meetings, 2 harnesses, 2 repeats; 12 runs with Qwen2.5 14B.
studies.finding_plain: A separate delivery decision produced 1 confirmed complete result out of 6, with 1 more uncertain. The baseline had none; errors and repeated updates remained.

studies.title: Understanding versus delivery
studies.sample_plain: 8 meeting prefixes, 2 models and 2 contexts; 32 recognition calls. Two meetings also had 3 paired continuation branches each.
studies.finding_plain: Saved history reduced diagnostic passes for both models. A correct need summary improved one meeting from 1 to 2 of 3 delivered conclusions; the other stayed at zero.
limits: Diagnostic context comparison is not a full-harness benchmark.
The correct summaries were supplied for diagnosis, not generated by an implemented memory method.
Six continuation branches did not achieve complete help; only two independent meetings were tested.
method_notes: Recognition compared human-only input with the same human dialogue plus saved assistant and tool history.
Continuation branches shared one checkpoint per meeting: unchanged, repeated human words, or a correct current-need summary.
The summary contained no factual answers or future dialogue, and inherited the remaining budget.
